warnings.text: Chainlink BTC/USD isn't recorded before 10 Nov 05:27 UTC: these windows have its start price and result only.

9 Nov 12:30 UTC window: no order book for 203 of 900 s; 882 of 1,170 market trades recorded.
10 Nov 00:00 UTC window: read from Polymarket's API, no order book; prices once a minute.

runs.text: Looking for what repeats across the windows.

runs.label: observed
runs.title: Buys before the window opens, usually both sides
runs.rule: Fills timed before the window's start (pre_open). Its first came 44 s, 23 s, 47 s early (3, 3, 7 fills before the open); both Up and Down before the open in 2 of 3; the 9 Nov 12:30 UTC window Down only.

runs.label: observed
runs.title: Holds both sides to the close, and lost in all 3 windows
runs.rule: Shares held of each side at the end, and profit from its fills plus the payout of shares held. 9 Nov 11:00 UTC window: 950 Up and 824 Down, resolved Down, −$46.61; 9 Nov 12:30 UTC window: 1,253 Up and 1,544 Down, resolved Up, −$55.59; 10 Nov 00:00 UTC window: 1,504 Up and 1,151 Down, resolved Down, −$74.23. Together −$176.43; merges and redemptions aren't in the fills.

runs.label: observed
runs.title: Most of its checked fills were resting buys, not taken at the asking price
runs.rule: A buy at or above the recorded best ask just before the trade paid the asking price; below it, a resting buy filled. In the 2 windows with a recorded book: 156 resting, 35 paid the asking price, 99 in recording gaps and not checked. The window without a book can't be checked.

runs.label: inferred
runs.title: It seems to quote both sides rather than pick a direction
runs.rule: If it rests buy orders on both Up and Down and keeps what fills to the close, most fills should sit below the asking price and both sides should be held at the end: 156 of 191 checked fills were resting buys, and all 3 windows ended holding both sides.
runs.would_change_mind: Fills mostly at the asking price in windows with a recorded book, or windows where it ends holding one side only.

runs.label: observed
runs.title: Spends more on Up than on Down: $1,190.00 on Up, $1,538.38 on Down
runs.rule: The fills' usd, buys only, by side.

Why does it buy below the asking price?.text: Counting its fills against the recorded book.

Why does it buy below the asking price?.label: How its fills compare with the asking price
observed: In the 2 windows with a recorded order book, 156 of its 191 checked fills were resting buys that filled, and 35 paid the asking price.
99 fills fell in recording gaps and can't be checked.
inferred: It seems to post buy orders a little below the asking price and wait to be filled, on both sides. If so, its fills should cluster just under the best ask; the windows with a recorded book are where that can be checked.
